correctness.rationale: For fixed actions a,b, the conformist score is p_i+1_{i=b}, while the rebel minimizes q_i+1_{i=a}; these exhaust all effects of the flexible edge. If Q has at least two members and is contained in P, a rebel best response lies in Q and makes the conformist copy it uniquely, after which the rebel strictly prefers another member of Q. Otherwise an explicit profile is a simultaneous best response: (a,b)=(maximum p, minimum q outside P), or, when Q is singleton in P, both choose its unique element. Integer one-unit strict gaps are checked at the boundary. Independent integer enumeration of 8,395 count-vector profiles and constructive witnesses passed; it is supplementary to the proof.

value.rationale: A local CR edge with stubborn influence is the atomic source of PNE failure used in recent network-game theory. Replacing a sufficient balanced-pin obstruction by an exact classification for all nonuniform pinned counts resolves a natural motivated local question. The theorem constructs equilibria on the other side of a sharp condition and supplies explicit nonuniform obstruction certificates on graphs outside the cited tree m>Delta classification. It does not overclaim a general network equilibrium criterion.
